question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 04 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The connection pool size change likely caused the increase in p95 latency.
why_chain: The auth db.pool_size was changed from 50 to 5.
This reduction in pool size means fewer connections are available to service requests.
With more requests than connections, the connection pool becomes exhausted, leading to increased latency.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in request volume could have contributed to the latency increase.
why_chain: The request volume for service auth increased by 23%.
With more requests, the connection pool becomes more strained.
Exhausted connections lead to increased latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was due to a sudden spike in user traffic.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume did not increase significantly, and the error rate increased instead.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was caused by a new deployment.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of a new deployment or version change.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for service auth rose from 91 ms to 253 ms (+179%), with a change point at 2026-03-04T12:00:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service auth: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.02).
At the same time, request volume for service auth stayed about the same (1097 per 5 min before, 1344 per 5 min after, +23%).
At the same time, error rate for service auth rose (0.35% before, 0.54% after, +55%).
Changed auth db.pool_size from 50 to 5 (all regions) (auth; 3 min before the change; record R019)
p95 latency above SLO on auth (auth; 15 min after the change; record R021)
auth: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (auth, ap-south; 13 min after the change; record R020)
auth: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (auth, eu-west; 19 min after the change; record R022)
auth: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (auth, us-east; 24 min after the change; record R023)

reasons: ✓ A change event (config_changes) lines up in time (3 min before the change).
✓ 4 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Increase the auth db.pool_size back to 50 to improve connection handling.
Monitor request volume and adjust the connection pool size as needed.
Review and optimize the connection pool size for future changes.
